title: Global leaders urged to join initiative to fight extreme inequality
content:
More than 1,500 academics and economists sign letter, calling growing gap between richest and poorest ‘a policy choice that can be reversed’

More than 1,500 academics and economists from 100-plus countries are urging global leaders to join an initiative against extreme inequality, calling current unfairness “a policy choice that can be reversed”.

Before the UN general assembly in New York next week, the experts have signed an open letter backing the International Panel on Inequality (IPI).
snippet: More than 1,500 academics and economists sign letter, calling growing gap between richest and poorest ‘a policy choice that can be reversed’
creator: Heather Stewart Economics editor

title: ‘A map is never neutral’: meet the cartographers who took on centuries of western bias
content:
Equal Earth projection, adopted by the UN last week, provides an alternative to 16th-century Mercator display

Three cartographers have spoken of their astonishment at the UN’s near-universal adoption of a map they created to more accurately show the sizes of Africa and Europe, even though they have received a few complaints from some disgruntled diplomats.

The creators of the Equal Earth projection aimed to provide an alternative to the dominant 16th-century Mercator display, which critics have long faulted for giving the impression that northern hemisphere nations are larger than they are – and therefore subtly reinforcing perceptions of where global strength lies.
snippet: Equal Earth projection, adopted by the UN last week, provides an alternative to 16th-century Mercator display
creator: Oliver Holmes, Ana Lucía González Paz and Pablo Gutiérrez
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Trump administration again denies entry visas to Palestinian officials ahead of UN general assembly
content:
For the second year in a row, the administration has barred the Palestinian delegation from US travel for the forum

The US state department said on Wednesday that it had again denied entry visas to Palestinian officials ahead next week’s United Nations general assembly gathering in New York.

The state department said in a statement the Palestinian Authority (PA) and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) had “failed to live up to their commitments”, accusing the groups of “taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ)” and of “glorifying terrorism” among other allegations.
snippet: For the second year in a row, the administration has barred the Palestinian delegation from US travel for the forum
creator: Anna Betts
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: a spur to action on climate | Editorial
content:
New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics

Following a familiar pattern, coverage of the glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border three weeks ago has subsided with the initial shock. But while the world’s attention has shifted, Nepal remains in the midst of an appalling tragedy. As well as at least 1,300 people who are known to have been killed, more than 5,000 are missing, some of them trapped in tunnels linked to the 13 hydropower plants that were damaged by the floods. On Wednesday four bodies were recovered from one of these tunnels, with searches ongoing. Families of the missing people are desperate for news.
snippet: New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics
creator: Editorial

title: Iran school bombing: grounds to believe US was behind atrocity, UN finds
content:
Fact-finding mission says military strikes on school and sports facility in ⁠February constitute war ⁠crimes

A UN fact-finding mission has determined there are reasonable grounds to believe the US was behind military strikes on a school and a sports facility in Iran in ⁠February that killed 120 children, and that these constituted war ⁠crimes.

The school strike, which killed 156 civilians including 120 children, involved a US Tomahawk missile that collapsed the roof of the Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school, which the UN said was “clearly identifiable”, in Minab, Hormozgan province, on 28 February.
snippet: Fact-finding mission says military strikes on school and sports facility in February constitute war crimes
creator: Peter Beaumont  and agencies
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Africa is bigger than we’ve been led to believe – what next?
content:
A new map of the world rescales the size of Africa and calls into question our perception of land, power and influence

This month, the UN passed a resolution, brought to the assembly by Togo, to phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe and replace it with another that shows the real scale of territories. That’s right – when it comes to size, the map of the world we have all grown up with is not accurate. The main loser of land on the Mercator map is Africa, and the new “Equal Earth” map reflects its true proportions. I spoke to our west Africa correspondent Eromo Egbejule about his extensive reporting on the map changes, and why people feel so strongly about it.

Seeing the new map transposed over the old might make you feel oddly disoriented. Logically, there is absolutely no immediate tangible impact on one’s life that comes out of knowing that the entire top part of the northern hemisphere is so much smaller than you were led to believe. And yet, there is still something agitating about it, like you’ve been the subject of a lifelong trick, or at least a breach of trust.
snippet: A new map of the world rescales the size of Africa and calls into question our perception of land, power and influence
creator: Nesrine Malik
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Burnham and Trump expected to meet for first time next week as PM steps up presence on world stage
content:
Andy Burnham will attend UN general assembly, where he is expected to try to drum up more support for Ukraine

Andy Burnham is expected to meet Donald Trump for the first time in person at the UN general assembly next week in New York.

Last month the Guardian reported British officials had stepped up their preparations for a face-to-face meeting between Burnham and Trump after the prime minister said he hoped to attend the assembly of world leaders.
snippet: Andy Burnham will attend UN general assembly, where he is expected to try to drum up more support for Ukraine
creator: Aletha Adu Political correspondent

title: Al-Qaida and IS-linked violence in Africa’s Sahel belt set to hit record levels this year
content:
Twenty-five years after 9/11, figures compiled by conflict monitor underline how Sahel region has become centre of Islamist terror

Islamist extremist violence in Africa’s Sahel region is set to reach historic highs after a series of sweeping offensives by groups linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State, according to new figures compiled by the conflict monitor Acled.

As the US marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks launched by al-Qaida against targets in Washington and New York, the statistics underline the continued expansion of the veteran organisation in parts of Africa – in stark contrast with its relative weakness elsewhere.
snippet: Twenty-five years after 9/11, figures compiled by conflict monitor underline how Sahel region has become centre of Islamist terror
creator: Jason Burke International security correspondent
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Houthis threaten more Saudi strikes as UN warns of humanitarian crisis in Yemen
content:
Estimated 100,000 Yemenis displaced amid renewed fighting as Qatar sounds alarm over Bab al-Mandab strait

Saudi cities faced the threat of a second day of Houthi attacks as fighting across Yemen led the UN to warn of a humanitarian crisis with 100,000 Yemenis already displaced.

As oil prices remained well over $100 (£74) a barrel, Qatar warned of a catastrophe if the Iran-backed Houthi militants won full control of the Bab al-Mandab strait, the narrow waterway at the bottom of the Red Sea dominating the key naval route to Asia. The strait has become vital to Saudi crude oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.
snippet: Estimated 100,000 Yemenis displaced amid renewed fighting as Qatar sounds alarm over Bab al-Mandab strait
creator: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor

title: Nearly 50,000 Yemeni civilians flee as Houthis advance along Red Sea coast
content:
Global struggle for control of Bab al-Mandab strait threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war

  • Violence erupts in Yemen again: why it matters globally and how it is linked to the US-Iran war

    • Violence erupts in Yemen again: why it matters globally and how it is linked to the US-Iran war

  • Saudi Arabia shuts down oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq

    • Saudi Arabia shuts down oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq

    Nearly 50,000 people have fled a sudden advance by Houthi forces in western Yemen, with entire villages emptied and families trapped near frontline fighting with depleting food supplies, according to aid workers.

    Civilians in the Middle East’s poorest country have found themselves victims of a global struggle for control over one of the most important shipping routes in the world, which threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war.
snippet: Global struggle for control of Bab al-Mandab strait threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war

title: UK minister warns of impact of Trump’s Iran war on next month’s budget
content:
Bridget Phillipson says Burnham’s past criticisms of US president not an issue as PM prepares to meet Trump at UN

Next month’s budget will be made more difficult by Donald Trump’s war with Iran, one of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said, while adding she did not expect the prime minister’s previous disparaging comments about the US president to be an issue.

Burnham is expected to meet Trump early next week at the UN general assembly summit in New York, the pair having previously spoken twice by phone since Burnham entered No 10.
snippet: Bridget Phillipson says Burnham’s past criticisms of US president not an issue as PM prepares to meet Trump at UN
creator: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent

title: Japan seeks change to new UN world map over Russia 'misconception'
content:
The new ‘true-scale’ map shrinks Europe and North America while enlarging Africa – and depicts the disputed Kuril islands as ruled by Moscow

Japan has asked for the revision of a new world map adopted by the UN because it said it made the disputed Kuril islands appear to belong to Russia.

The UN general assembly voted on Friday to adopt the new map, which makes the African continent larger while also shrinking North America and Europe, drawing condemnation from the US.
snippet: The new ‘true-scale’ map shrinks Europe and North America while enlarging Africa – and depicts the disputed Kuril islands as ruled by Moscow
creator: Agence France-Presse in Tokyo
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster
content:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions

Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.

Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.
snippet: Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions
creator: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Kathmandu
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Heatwaves and wildfires are setting back air quality improvements, UN finds
content:
WMO report details extreme weather events causing climatic feedback loop with serious health consequences

Big increases in wildfires and heatwaves supercharged by the climate crisis are hindering improvements to air quality around the world, UN experts have said.

Regions that had recorded a fall in pollution emitted by cars and industrial sites are facing new threats to air quality because of exposure to smoke from wildfires, according to a new report, while rising temperatures caused by intense heatwaves are causing a surge in ground-level ozone.
snippet: WMO report details extreme weather events causing climatic feedback loop with serious health consequences
creator: Damien Gayle
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: UN votes to adopt new world map that shows Africa’s true scale
content:
Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland

The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.

In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favour of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.
snippet: Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland
creator: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Minister tells Brits to stock up on days of supplies after ‘supersize’ El Niño warning
content:
Exclusive: Angela Eagle urges UK citizens to be ‘a bit more resilient’ as they plan for national emergencies

British people have been urged to have enough food and water on hand to survive a few days without power or water, as the UN said the El Niño climate phenomenon was “supersizing before our eyes”, exacerbating extreme weather events worldwide.

Forecasters say they are braced for the biggest El Niño in 1,000 years, bringing wildfires and floods to parts of the world, and the threat of a wet, stormy winter for the UK.

As the British government plans a campaign urging citizens to prepare for national emergencies, Angela Eagle told the Guardian the likelihood of a wild winter showed the importance of keeping supplies at home.
snippet: Exclusive: Angela Eagle urges UK citizens to be ‘a bit more resilient’ as they plan for national emergencies
creator: Kiran Stacey and Damian Carrington
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Grinding up fish to feed to fish is ‘absurd’: fears over UN aquaculture plan
content:
Huge rollout of fish farms could harm ecosystems and threaten vulnerable communities’ food sources, say experts

Nearly half of the world’s wild fish catch will be ground into animal feed for farmed fish if plans to expand aquaculture go ahead, a report has found.

The UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is aiming to increase aquaculture – where fish are farmed rather than caught in the wild – production by 75% by 2040, according to its sustainable development goal roadmap.
snippet: Huge rollout of fish farms could harm ecosystems and threaten vulnerable communities’ food sources, say experts
creator: Matthew Pearce
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: Countries legally obliged to consider slavery reparations, says UN committee
content:
Guidance says states must implement ‘comprehensive measures’ to address legacy of racial discrimination

A UN committee has said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other ⁠measures to address the enduring ⁠legacy of racial ​discrimination.

Guidance published on Monday by the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination (CERD) said the obligations arose from ⁠a legally binding 1965 convention on racial discrimination, not from the legal standards that existed when the slave trade took place.
snippet: Guidance says states must implement ‘comprehensive measures’ to address legacy of racial discrimination
creator: Reuters in Geneva
sourceDescription: Latest news and features from theguardian.com, the world's leading liberal voice

title: ‘Breakthrough’ as Turkmenistan starts fixing ‘mindboggling’ methane mega-leaks
content:
Secretive state begins repairs on ageing facilities after being revealed as worst country for leaks of potent greenhouse gas

Turkmenistan has started plugging the mega-leaks of methane that spew from its ageing oil and gas facilities, the latest UN data shows, in a move hailed as a breakthrough.

Methane, also called natural or fossil gas, is a potent greenhouse gas. It traps 80 times more heat than carbon dioxide and causes 25% of global heating today. Stopping leaks can be quick and cheap and, because methane breaks down in the atmosphere far quicker than CO2, this has a rapid impact, with some experts calling it the climate “emergency brake”.
snippet: Secretive state begins repairs on ageing facilities after being revealed as worst country for leaks of potent greenhouse gas
creator: Damian Carrington Environment editor

title: Trump’s deep-sea mining plan flouts international law | Letter
content:
Britain and other signatories to the UN convention on the law of the sea should protest against US proposal to lease seabed for mining, says Guy Standing

Your article on Donald Trump’s plan to lease millions of hectares of seabed in the Pacific for deep-sea mining correctly points to the ecological disaster that this could unleash (US territories hit out at Trump plan to explore deep sea mining in the Pacific, 24 August).

However, it does not mention that this plan contravenes international law in the form of Unclos, the UN convention on the law of the sea, which has been ratified by 171 countries and the European Union. The US has not ratified it, but since 1982 has agreed to abide by its rules and procedures.
snippet: Britain and other signatories to the UN convention on the law of the sea should protest against US proposal to lease seabed for mining, says Guy Standing
creator: Guardian Staff
